_readme: Recorded highlight/analysis/podcast/etc. channels for the 'Videos' tab (see js/videos.js). Unlike streams.json, this section is NOT gated behind a live basho — it shows all the time.
Schema per entry: { id, label, channelUrl, channelId, category, contentType, official, language, status, communityRank, disabled, note }.
channelUrl    plain https://www.youtube.com/@handle URL — always required; used as the 'open channel' link and as the fallback card when there's no embed.
channelId     YouTube's UC... internal channel ID — optional. When present, embeds that channel's uploads playlist (auto-updates, nothing to maintain). null when not yet confirmed.
category      one of: Livestream, Official, Highlights, Analysis, Podcast, Organization, Club, Stable — drives the category filter chips in the UI.
contentType   free text, shown as a small subtitle on the card (e.g. 'Daily Highlights').
official      true for official broadcaster/JSA/stable/organization channels — drives the 'Official only' filter.
language      'en' or 'ja' — drives the language filter.

status        'Active' | 'Occasional' | 'Intermittent' | 'Historical'. Entries with status 'Historical' are hidden by default (js/videos.js) — the person can reveal them via Settings > Show inactive channels. This is separate from 'disabled', which is a hard, non-toggleable gate for entries this app can't safely show at all (unconfirmed handle, not embeddable, etc).
communityRank lower is more prominent within its category, per community round-ups (r/Sumo etc.) circa mid-2026 — used as a sort key, not a hard cutoff. null when unranked.
disabled      true keeps an entry out of the rendered grid entirely, regardless of settings — for unverified handles or channels this app can't embed. 'note' explains why.

On every load, js/videos.js pings each *enabled* YouTube entry's uploads-playlist via YouTube's public oEmbed endpoint (the same CORS-friendly, keyless mechanism streams.js already uses for live-detection) and hides any that no longer resolve, so a taken-down channel doesn't sit there as a broken embed. It can't tell you *why* a channel is unreachable (deleted vs. renamed vs. temporary API hiccup) — if a channel goes missing from the grid, check data/videos.json's channelId/channelUrl by hand before assuming the worst. This check can't run for Twitch/Rumble/website entries (no public CORS-friendly way to ask), so those still need periodic manual review.

Ranking/description text is loosely based on community round-ups (r/Sumo, watch guides) circa mid-2026, plus a CSV list the site owner compiled themselves — treat both as a starting point, not gospel. 'ReliabilityScore'/'DiscoveryScore' as concepts (mentioned in the site owner's original filtering brief) aren't implemented: there's no analytics source feeding real values for those, and fabricating numbers would be worse than not having them. The sort order in js/videos.js approximates the same *intent* (official + well-established + currently active first) using the real fields above (official, communityRank, status) instead.

videos.label: Sumo Jason (Jason's All-Sumo Channel)
videos.note: Same creator as the older 'Jason's All-Sumo Channel' / youtube.com/user/JasonsinJapan URL — kept as one entry rather than a duplicate.

videos.label: Sumo Video — JSA Official Channel
videos.note: This is literally the Japan Sumo Association's own channel (confirmed via its About page: '日本相撲協会公式チャンネル'), so marked official:true even though the source CSV had it as No.

videos.label: NHK WORLD-JAPAN
videos.note: General NHK World channel, not sumo-exclusive, but the official broadcaster and the source of sumo highlights/occasional live coverage. Also listed in streams.json for its occasional live sumo broadcasts.

videos.label: Kintamayama
videos.note: Original channel taken down Jan 2023, a follow-up channel also deleted; briefly on Rumble (https://rumble.com/user/Kintamayama). This channel displays as 'Mordy Dunchy' with no sumo content in its About section, but the site owner confirmed directly this is the same, rebranded channel/handle.

videos.label: Natto Sumo
videos.note: Repeatedly hit by copyright takedowns and has moved channels/platforms more than once historically — this handle was confirmed live via its own About page while building this feature, but it's worth keeping an eye on given the history.

videos.label: Sumo Scott (formerly World of Sumo)
videos.note: Rebranded from 'World of Sumo' to 'Sumo Scott' at some point — the @WorldOfSumo handle now 404s. Confirmed via the channel's own About page, which explicitly says 'formerly World of Sumo'.

videos.label: Hooked On Sumo
videos.note: Handle matches the site owner's CSV, status Historical (inactive) per that same list, and channelId not independently confirmed — verify before enabling.

videos.label: 42 Opinions Sumo
videos.note: Even the site owner's own research only turned up a YouTube search-results URL, not a confirmed channel — left disabled until an actual channel is found.
